Header: 2026-03-07 15:00 UTC — Duration 45m
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood Partnerships), Olivia Mendes (Stratagem Partnerships), Marco Silva (Solutions Architect), Jinwoo Park (Head of Integrations), Sara Lopez (Security)

Summary: quick partner intro + high-level integration feasibility. Discussed dedicated vs hosted routing, private control-plane options, security (SOC2/KMS), and next steps for benching.

Topics: partner model (reselling/integration), runtime compatibility, VPC/on-prem options, KMS & audit logs, expected throughput, pilot scope, commercial motion

[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on the partner program. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer, and Maya from partnerships.
[00:12] Olivia: Hi all, Olivia here. Excited to learn more, we chatted a bit over email.
[00:18] Marco: Marco joining, we'll probably talk infra and integration details — I'm the solutions architect.
[00:24] Jinwoo: Jinwoo here, head of integrations. We'll look at what the embed / reseller flow looks like.
[00:30] Ethan: Great. Very high level — Redwood does hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC / on-prem) installs. We aim to make serving consistent whether you're calling our hosted flow or running private.
[00:44] Priya: Yeah quick note on runtime — our serving engine manages KV cache, continuous batching, and kernel selection for different GPUs. For partner integrations we often recommend starting with hosted for ease then move to dedicated pools for predictable throughput.
[00:58] Marco: When you say KV cache you mean the key-value cache? Sometimes I see docs say K-V cash in older exports — just clarifying.
[01:08] Priya: Yes KV cache, sorry transcription, K-V cash ha — it's the same. Helps with prefix reuse and reduces token cost for repeated contexts.
[01:18] Olivia: On commercial model: are you expecting partners to resell Redwood hosted API, or run a dedicated co-branded stack?
[01:29] Ethan: We support both. Typical flows: 1) resell calls to our hosted API with partner rate cards, 2) joint dedicated pools where partner offers managed capacity, and 3) private deployments where the partner provides a private control plane to large enterprise customers.
[01:44] Marco: For the private option, is the control plane fully customer-managed? We have some regulated customers who require that.
[01:52] Priya: For Private we offer a control plane that can be customer-managed (VPC + optional on-prem package). You can bring your KMS/HSM for key management, and we emit audit logs to your SIEM. There are a few templated deployment patterns.
[02:06] Sara: SOC 2 is important for us. Can you share your attestation? Also SSO options — SAML, OIDC?
[02:15] Ethan: Yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO work in progress; we'll share the artifact. SSO via SAML and OIDC supported, RBAC with fine-grained roles. We'll drop the security pack after this call.
[02:28] Olivia: Great. What about model catalog — partners often want a stable list of verified models and performance numbers so we can recommend to customers.
[02:36] Priya: We maintain a catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified perf profiles (latency / cost) — I can share a sample CSV and the perf dashboards. Note sometimes model names differ across infra, so there is mapping needed (e.g., 'rw-bert-v2' vs other vendor names).
[02:52] Marco: Benchmarks — if we want to run comparison tests on our hardware against hosted, is there an easy way to do that? Do you support runbook or test harness?
[03:00] Priya: Yes we have a benchmark harness and a sample payload set. For partners we usually run a joint benchmark: 1) sample workload, 2) target latency percentiles, 3) cost per token comparisons, 4) accuracy checks. We'll prepare a plan.
[03:12] Jinwoo: On the networking side, does Redwood require inbound ports? Do you do egress only outbound? How does private peering work?
[03:19] Priya: For hosted it's egress to our API endpoints. Private deployments can be peered into your VPC or run on-prem with the control plane talking over mutual TLS. We'll capture diagrams — Marco, if you share your VPC topology we can map it.
[03:33] Marco: Sure. We'll share diagrams after the call.
[03:36] Ethan: Quick commercial note — for dedicated reserved capacity we do monthly/annual commits. For partners reselling hosted API, there are partner rate cards and margin tiers. We'll share a high level commercial model doc.
[03:49] Olivia: Any limitations around model sizes or GPU types for private deployments?
[03:54] Priya: We support a range, but some large models require specific kernels and GPU memory profiles. We have quantized variants too. For example 4-bit quantization on A100 or H100 variants is common. Occasionally model perf varies by architecture and kernel availability.
[04:10] Marco: Do you support M-series or just NVIDIA? We have customers looking to run on AMD MI or upcoming M-series.
[04:17] Priya: Currently primary public support is NVIDIA (A100, H100). We have partners running on AMD but some kernel work is needed. We can roadmap support for M-series if there's demand.
[04:27] Sara: Audit logs: how long are logs retained? Can we ship to our Splunk/Datadog?
[04:34] Ethan: Logs can be exported to your SIEM; retention depends on plan — enterprise customers can configure retention windows and export. We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:45] Olivia: On latency vs cost tradeoffs — what controls do we have? Batching, caching, and quantization you mentioned — any auto-suggest features?
[04:55] Priya: Yes Redwood Optimize suggests batching and quant configs by workload; it also recommends model variants for cost/perf balance. There is a routing policy so you can route latency-sensitive calls to premium pools and batch jobs to cheaper variants.
[05:09] Marco: For customers who want deterministic latency, is dedicated the recommended path?
[05:14] Priya: Yes dedicated reserved pools provide predictable throughput and SLOs. Hosted has multi-tenant variability but we do prioritization for enterprise tiers.
[05:23] Jinwoo: Integration surface: we will embed calls inside our control plane to route to Redwood or partner-hosted endpoints. Do you provide SDKs or is it raw REST only?
[05:31] Ethan: We have REST + official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. We also support streaming and function/tool calling patterns.
[05:38] Olivia: Any embargo or exclusivity considerations for partners?
[05:42] Maya: We don't generally require exclusivity; focus is on joint GTM motion. We do have co-marketing tiers for preferred partners.
[05:49] Marco: For the bench plan — can you give a quick example of metrics you'd collect?
[05:54] Priya: Sure: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, memory RPS, error rates, and quality regressions on a sample eval set. We'll also track warm vs cold KV cache behavior.
[06:07] Olivia: About model variants — do you auto-fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained? We need that for reliability.
[06:13] Priya: Yes smart routing can fallback to compatible variants based on policy. You can set policy by latency or cost tiers.
[06:22] Jinwoo: Do you handle data residency? Some customers need EU-only storage.
[06:27] Ethan: Yes hosted endpoints are regioned; private deployments let you keep data in your control plane / storage. We'll note data residency options in the follow-up pack.
[06:36] Marco: Onbench testing — would Redwood run tests on our hardware or we run tests and send results?
[06:42] Priya: Either. For private deployments we can provide the harness and run tests with your infra team, or you can run locally and share metrics. For partners we often do joint runs to validate performance.
[06:53] Olivia: Security question — do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with an HSM?
[06:58] Ethan: Yes BYOK via supported KMS/HSM integrations is available for Private and Enterprise Dedicated customers.
[07:06] Sara: Logging and redaction — can we mask PII before it leaves our VPC?
[07:12] Priya: We support client-side redaction patterns and server-side hooks. If you need strict PII control, private deploy + customer-managed logs is the safest.
[07:23] Marco: Any known gotchas when integrating with partner control planes?
[07:28] Priya: A few: model kernel mismatches, firewall/NAT traversal for on-prem control plane, and KV cache warm-up behavior. We document best practices and have runbooks for common issues.
[07:40] Ethan: Okay let's talk timelines. Olivia, what's your typical partner onboarding timeline?
[07:45] Olivia: For strategic partners we try to do an intro + tech deep dive within 2 weeks and a pilot within 4-6 weeks, depending on customer commitments.
[07:55] Ethan: Sounds good — we can aim for a tech deep-dive the week of Mar 15. Priya will prepare the bench plan.
[08:02] Maya: We'll also loop in the partnerships PM to discuss co-marketing and deal registration.
[08:08] Olivia: Commercially, we need indicative margin and pricing to present to our biz dev.
[08:13] Ethan: We'll send a partner commercial overview and partner rate cards.
[08:17] Marco: One last quick question on SLA: what are your uptime and latency SLOs for dedicated pools?
[08:23] Priya: Typical SLA for dedicated is 99.9% with latency targets depending on model and pool type. We'll include concrete numbers in the follow-up.
[08:32] Jinwoo: Is there any sandbox environment we can use for dev/test?
[08:36] Ethan: Yes we provide sandbox keys and limited credit for integration testing.
[08:40] Olivia: Ok good.
[08:42] Ethan: Cool — recap and next steps: we'll send partner deck + security pack (SOC2, SAML docs), Priya will send benchmark plan, Stratagem to share network/topology and expected throughput, and we'll schedule a tech deep dive week of Mar 15.
[08:57] Marco: Sounds good — thanks everyone.
[09:00] Olivia: Thanks.
[09:02] Jinwoo: Thanks.
